name: Axiom Systems TouchShield TS-3 'Porcupine'
description:
An adhesive-backed electrical discharge patch that can be applied to clothing, bags, or directly to skin, delivering a 55,000-volt shock to anyone who touches the protected surface. The TS-3 is a thin, flexible circuit printed on a polymer substrate with a pressure-sensitive trigger — any contact pressure above 500 grams activates the discharge. The user's own skin is insulated by the adhesive backing, while the outer surface is the active electrode.

Axiom Systems markets the TS-3 as passive defense — protection that works even when the user cannot actively respond. Patches are commonly applied to purse straps, jacket shoulders, backpack handles, and anywhere a pickpocket or grab-attacker is likely to make contact. The patches are disposable, with each containing a single-discharge capacitor that depletes on first activation. They are sold in packs of five for Φ60.

The TS-3 has found unexpected popularity among delivery workers and couriers who are frequently targeted for their cargo. Applied to the handles of delivery containers, the patches deter grab-and-run theft with painful consistency. The primary limitation is single-use — once triggered, the patch is spent and must be replaced. Axiom is developing a rechargeable variant, but the current disposable model dominates the market.
specifications:
voltage: 55,000V
amperage: 2.8 milliamps
trigger threshold: 500 grams contact pressure
uses: single discharge per patch
patch dimensions: 5 cm x 5 cm
thickness: 0.4 mm
weight: 3 g per patch
cost: Φ60 for 5-pack
shelf life: 18 months
tactical_use: Apply patches to surfaces most likely to be grabbed during an attack — bag straps, collar area, wrist cuffs, wallet pockets. The TS-3 is a deterrent, not an incapacitator — the shock is painful and surprising but brief. Its value is in discouraging follow-up grabs after the first contact. For maximum coverage, apply multiple patches to different grab points. Replace triggered patches promptly — a spent patch is just a sticker.
cultural_context: The TS-3 has introduced the concept of 'passive defense zoning' to personal security — making your own body and belongings a hazard to touch without permission. This idea resonates strongly in a city where personal space is constantly violated by crowds, predators, and opportunists. Some Tier 1-2 residents apply patches to their children's school bags and jackets, normalizing from a young age the idea that one's body and property should be defended even passively.
story_hooks: A Tier 2 market vendor has been found applying TS-3 patches to merchandise to prevent shoplifting — a customer with a pacemaker was hospitalized after handling a patched product, raising questions about liability when passive defense harms innocent people.

Someone has developed bootleg TS-3 patches with dramatically increased voltage that are being sold as genuine — the counterfeits are visually identical but deliver discharges that cause burns and tissue damage.

physical_description.visual_profile: A thin, almost translucent square patch resembling a circuit board sticker. At first glance, it appears inert — a piece of tech no more threatening than a diagnostic label. The outer surface displays fine copper tracery etched across a pale polymer base, with contact points visible at the edges. Deceptively flat and mundane, but the copper pathways hint at its electrical nature.
physical_description.dimensions: 5 cm x 5 cm square, 0.4 mm thickness
physical_description.weight_description: Negligible — weighs only 3 grams. So light it's almost unnoticeable once adhered to fabric or skin. No heft whatsoever; the patch clings like a second skin.
physical_description.primary_material: Flexible polymer substrate (likely PET or polyimide) with printed copper circuit traces and a pressure-sensitive adhesive backing
physical_description.finish: Matte translucent polymer face with metallic copper circuitry visible beneath. The adhesive side is glossy and slightly tacky to the touch. No reflection — designed to be inconspicuous.
physical_description.color_scheme: Off-white or pale cream polymer base with bright copper-gold circuit traces. Minimal branding — subtle gray Axiom Systems lettering in one corner. The reverse side shows the adhesive as a faint amber tint.
physical_description.grip_texture: Not gripped — applied as an adhesive patch. The polymer face is smooth and slightly waxy. The backing is pressure-sensitive and tacky, adhering firmly to fabric or skin without requiring activation to stick.
distinctive_features: Etched copper electrode pathways forming concentric circuit patterns
Pressure-sensitive contact points along the outer edge
Tiny capacitor reservoir visible as a raised nodule in the center
Minimal Axiom Systems branding — intentionally low-profile
Fine copper traces that shimmer faintly under light, hinting at electrical charge
Matte finish prevents reflection and glare — designed to blend into bags and clothing
Razor-thin profile allows seamless adhesion to straps, collars, and curved surfaces
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Axiom Systems logo (small, 3-4mm) in gray printed text at the bottom right corner. Serial batch number printed in micro-font along one edge. Instruction symbols for activation threshold printed in white ink beneath the logo.
physical_description.condition_typical: Fresh patches appear pristine and uniform — manufactured to exacting standards. In the field, patches waiting for deployment show no visible wear. Post-activation patches appear charred or discolored at the contact point where the arc occurred, rendering them obviously spent. Used patches are typically discarded or replaced within hours.
